transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Um... I guess my wife and my director at work told me I needed to come. I just... I can't really stop starting things right now. 

Projects, I mean. Work plans, scheduling new certifications... tearing apart the home network to upgrade it. Even just messaging old contacts. It gets... intense, I guess. I kind of blow past normal limits until one of them has to step in and stop me. So... that's why I'm here.
How much have you been sleeping lately?

Not much, really. Um... there have been these runs lately where I only get maybe three hours. I'll wake up sharp at 3 or 4 a.m. and... I don't feel tired at all. It just feels like I've been handed bonus time to get things done.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t?

Um... I guess. Sometimes. 

It's mostly just... when I'm alone. In my home office, or if I'm around the server-room hum at work. The noise kind of... I don't know. I'll hear my name. Or just short comments. Like, someone saying "check the logs," or... "they know." 

But it's only when nobody else is in there with me. So... yeah.
When you hear those comments or your name, do you believe they are actually real and coming from someone or something outside your mind?

I don't really know. 

I mean... it sounds real when it happens. It sounds like someone is standing right behind me. But then I look, and... nobody's there. So... I guess I'm not sure.
Have you ever had a period of at least a week when your mood was abnormally elevated or irritable and you had these symptoms, but no hallucinations or delusions at all?

Um... no, I don't think so. 

Whenever I get into those really driven stretches... where I'm barely sleeping and trying to push through huge plans at work... that's usually when I hear those comments in the server noise. And... I start reading hidden threats into my work messages, too. 

So... no. It kind of all happens at the same time.
Have you ever had a time when you were hearing or believing those things even though your mood was otherwise normal?

Um... yeah. I guess so. 

There have been stretches like that. Just... calm, or flat. Maybe for a few weeks at a time, where I wasn't feeling particularly up or depressed. 

But... I still heard those brief comments. And... I still felt like the Teams statuses at work were coded warnings. So... yeah. It happens then, too.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt clearly depressed or lost interest in almost everything?

Yeah... I suppose. 

There are stretches where I just... wake up feeling pretty heavy. Just flat. Like I'm a... a failed version of myself, I guess. 

When it gets like that, even just answering my wife's normal questions feels like it's... too much. So... yeah. I've had times like that.
Have there ever been times when you were hearing or believing those things for at least two weeks while you were not having any manic or depressed symptoms at all?

Um... yeah. Like I just said... there have been a few weeks at a time where things were just flat. 

I wasn't feeling heavy or... or driven. Just normal, I guess. But... I still thought the Teams statuses meant something. And I still heard those comments. So... yes. For a few weeks at a time.
Have you ever had a period of at least one week where your mood was clearly abnormally elevated or irritable and you had more energy than usual?

Um... yeah, I guess. 

There are weeks where I just feel... I don't know, kind of electric. Like I can't be stopped. I just have a lot of energy. 

But then... if there's a small delay with something, or my wife asks me a question... I just snap. It's like everyone is just trying to slow me down on purpose. So... yeah, I get irritable then.
During those times when you feel especially electric or irritable, have they ever caused such serious problems that you could not function normally or needed hospitalization?

Yeah... I guess you could say that. 

I, um... I was put on leave at work. We had this big migration project and it... well, it failed. So they made me take some time off. 

And at home... it's been hard. My wife has had to step in a lot. Just... managing the money, trying to stop me from working all night, dealing with me when I start arguing over nothing. 

I don't really do much else anymore. I used to play music at church, go climbing, do some mentoring... but I just stopped. I couldn't really... follow through with any of it. So, yeah. It causes problems.
Have you ever had hallucinations or fixed false beliefs for at least two weeks when your mood was otherwise normal?

I thought I just... yeah, I said that already. There have been times. Just... flat stretches. Calm, I guess. A few weeks at a time where I wasn't really up or down. But I still thought the Teams statuses were warnings. And I still heard those comments. So, yes.
Have there ever been times when the hearing the comments or believing the Teams messages were warnings lasted at least two weeks while you were not having any manic or depressed symptoms?

I... I think I just answered this. But, yes. Like I said, there were stretches of time... a few weeks at a time, where things were just calm. I wasn't really up, and I wasn't depressed. Just flat. 

But I still thought the Teams statuses were coded warnings. And I still heard those brief comments, even when no one was in the room. So... yes. It lasted a few weeks like that.

Have you ever had a period of at least one week where you felt clearly abnormally elevated or irritable and had much more energy than usual, but without any hallucinations or fixed false beliefs during that time?

I... no, I don't think so. Not really. 

When I get like that—when I'm barely sleeping and just... pushing everything, working on the big plans—that's usually when it happens. The other stuff, I mean. I'll be really driven, but I'll still hear those comments in the server noise. And I'll still be seeing the threats in the messages. 

So... no. They kind of happen together.
Before these symptoms started, were you functioning pretty much normally at work and at home?

Well, before all this started, yes, I was doing fine. But lately... no. 

I was actually put on leave from work. The server migration failed, and... yeah. They told me to take time off. 

At home, it's been hard. My wife has had to step in a lot. Mostly with the spending, and trying to stop me from working all night. We end up arguing a lot. 

I don't really do much else anymore, either. I used to play music at church, go climbing, mentor some junior guys... but I've pulled away from all of it. I just can't seem to follow through or show up when I'm supposed to. So, things have definitely changed.
Have there ever been any hallucinations or fixed false beliefs that continued for at least two weeks while you were clearly having no manic or depressive symptoms at all?

I thought we... didn't we just cover this? 

Yeah, I mean... like I said earlier. There were a few weeks where things were just flat. Calm, I guess. I wasn't up, wasn't down. But I still thought the statuses were warnings. And I still heard those comments. So, yes.
Have there ever been any periods when the hearing the comments or believing the Teams messages were warnings continued for at least two weeks while your mood was completely normal?

Yeah... um, like I just said. Yes. 

There have been several stretches like that. A few weeks at a time where things were just flat, or calm. I wasn't up, and I wasn't depressed. But... I still believed the Teams statuses were coded warnings. And I would still hear those brief comments when no one was around. 

So... yes.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing or believing those things, but you were not having any manic symptoms at all?

I... yes. I feel like we just went over this. 

Like I said, there were stretches for a few weeks where I wasn't manic. I wasn't up at all. Just flat, or calm. But I still thought the Teams statuses were warnings... and I still heard those comments. 

So, yes. I don't really know what else to add to that.
Have there been any times when you were having those voices or warning beliefs while you were also clearly manic or depressed?

Yeah... um, yes. 

When things were at their most... intense. You know, when I was barely sleeping and trying to push all those big projects through. I was still... I was hearing the comments then, too. Like, in the noise from the servers. And I was still seeing the threats in the messages. 

So, yes. Both at the same time.
Have the voices or warning beliefs ever lasted for at least two weeks when you were not having any manic or depressive symptoms?

I... we just talked about this. I've answered this three times now. 

Yes. There were a few weeks where I wasn't up or down. Just flat. But I still heard the comments and saw the warnings on Teams. 

I don't know why we keep going in circles with this.
Have you ever had a full depressive episode that lasted at least two weeks?

I suppose. There are... stretches. Like, maybe a couple of weeks at a time where I just wake up feeling heavy. Flat. Like I'm just a failed version of myself. It gets to where even answering my wife's normal questions just feels like too much effort. So, yeah, I guess I've had that.

target_item.manifestation: There have been several calm or flat stretches, including a few weeks at a time, when I wasn’t especially up or depressed but still believed Teams statuses were coded warnings and still heard brief comments when no one was there.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking again if the psychotic symptoms (hearing/believing things) occurred for at least two weeks without manic symptoms, which refers to the requirement of psychotic symptoms in the absence of a major mood episode.

patient.answer:
I... yes. I feel like we just went over this. 

Like I said, there were stretches for a few weeks where I wasn't manic. I wasn't up at all. Just flat, or calm. But I still thought the Teams statuses were warnings... and I still heard those comments. 

So, yes. I don't really know what else to add to that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether psychotic symptoms occur exclusively during mood episodes or persist independently, which separates schizoaffective disorder from bipolar I disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: Have there been any times when you were having those voices or warning beliefs while you were also clearly manic or depressed?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: During my most driven stretches, when I was barely sleeping and pushing huge plans, I was also hearing comments in the server noise and reading hidden threats into work messages.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the psychotic symptoms (voices, warning beliefs) occurred at the same time as a manic or depressive episode, which maps to the requirement that psychotic symptoms and mood episodes occur concurrently.

patient.answer:
Yeah... um, yes. 

When things were at their most... intense. You know, when I was barely sleeping and trying to push all those big projects through. I was still... I was hearing the comments then, too. Like, in the noise from the servers. And I was still seeing the threats in the messages. 

So, yes. Both at the same time.

doctor.intent: Determine whether psychotic symptoms are present only during mood episodes versus also occurring independently, to distinguish schizoaffective disorder from bipolar I disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: Have the voices or warning beliefs ever lasted for at least two weeks when you were not having any manic or depressive symptoms?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: There have been several calm or flat stretches, including a few weeks at a time, when I wasn’t especially up or depressed but still believed Teams statuses were coded warnings and still heard brief comments when no one was there.
target_item.reason: The doctor is again asking if the psychotic symptoms (voices and warning beliefs) occurred for at least two weeks in the absence of manic or depressive symptoms (major mood episode).

patient.answer:
I... we just talked about this. I've answered this three times now. 

Yes. There were a few weeks where I wasn't up or down. Just flat. But I still heard the comments and saw the warnings on Teams. 

I don't know why we keep going in circles with this.

doctor.intent: To determine whether there has been a major depressive episode independent of the psychotic symptoms, which would support schizoaffective disorder over bipolar I disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: Have you ever had a full depressive episode that lasted at least two weeks?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: There are stretches where I wake up feeling like a failed version of myself, just heavy and flat, and even answering my wife’s normal questions feels like too much.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the presence of a full depressive episode, which corresponds to the symptom of depressed mood.

patient.answer: I suppose. There are... stretches. Like, maybe a couple of weeks at a time where I just wake up feeling heavy. Flat. Like I'm just a failed version of myself. It gets to where even answering my wife's normal questions just feels like too much effort. So, yeah, I guess I've had that.

opening_question.intent: Open the interview and elicit the patient’s main concern in their own words.
opening_question.question: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has clear manic syndrome with decreased need for sleep, increased goal-directed activity, pressured/driven behavior, irritability, and marked functional impairment. He also has persistent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persecutory ideas) that occur during mood episodes and, critically, continue for several weeks during periods when mood is neither manic nor depressed. This establishes schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type rather than bipolar I disorder with psychotic features, because psychosis is present for at least 2 weeks outside mood episodes.
